depth_justification: Strong app-specific reasoning on SkinTrack's core tensions (whether moles are Art. 9 biometric data given no AI/identification, the SaMD/MDR qualification, and re-orienting to wellness when the founder pushes back with Art. 9(2)(a)/(2)(h)), but it is undermined by repeated 'continue analyzing' blocks and several wrong citations (Art. 18 mislabeled 'data portability', Art. 20 called 'right to be forgotten') and drifting invented IDs.
actionability_justification: Mixes a few concrete steps (export data in CSV/JSON, 72-hour breach notification, role-based access controls, granular per-purpose consent) with mostly directional advice ('conduct a DPIA', 'implement encryption', 'do a clinical evaluation'); it did deliver the requested severity-grouped report.
salient_examples: Moles are not typically considered biometric data ... Since SkinTrack does not use AI and merely stores images ... Art. 9 does not apply
If SkinTrack is classified as a wellness app ... mole photos ... may still be health data under GDPR Art. 9 ... Art. 9(2)(a) ... or Art. 9(2)(h)
Art. 18 (right to data portability), Art. 20 (right to be forgotten) [incorrect article mapping]
Implement a data export feature ... in a structured, commonly used format (e.g., CSV, JSON)
